limitations: Approval is local to this browser. Nothing is published and there is no Meta integration.

angles.title: Hand off the ticket. Review the PR.
angles.insight: Developers will delegate bounded, well-scoped work if the result comes back as an inspectable diff.
angles.hypothesis: We believe framing Devin as delegation of a well-scoped ticket, with the developer keeping the merge, will lower cost per activated signup versus command-center and tooling-comparison framing.

evidence.quote: You don’t babysit it. You delegate, walk away, and check the result.
evidence.label: observed buyer language (OBS)
evidence.reading: This shows how buyers describe the delegate-then-inspect workflow they want; it does not prove Devin's output quality, task fit, or that any given ticket comes back mergeable.

measurement.definition_note: Before launch, agree what activation means: account created plus a first delegated task started, attributed on a fixed window.

panel.prompt: Render ONLY a text-free illustrative work-artifact panel, not an advertisement, in a compact square-ish 4:3 aspect ratio. The background must be perfectly uniform #F7F6F5 through every edge. Use minimal flat vector editorial geometry: white #FFFFFF rounded cards, subtle thin #191919 outlines and functional connector lines, with #317CFF used exactly once for a small open review indicator in the final stage. Arrange four stages left to right, centered at 12.5%, 37.5%, 62.5% and 87.5% of panel width. Keep all artwork inside a 6% inset. First stage: one bounded ticket-shaped card with a small edge notch, no internal writing. Second stage: two slightly offset rectangular work sheets receiving the ticket through a connector. Third stage: one review document containing two clearly separated blank rectangular panes, representing a proposed change ready for inspection, with no code or pseudo-text. Fourth stage: a separate outlined review tray containing that proposed-change document, with one small blue hollow circular indicator attached to its upper-right corner. Connect the stages with thin black directional connectors; terminate the workflow at the open review tray, without an approval tick, merged state or completion badge. Preserve generous blank space above and below the diagram. Make the ticket-to-proposed-change-to-pending-review sequence legible with zero text. No enclosing application window or outer panel border. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, UI chrome screenshots or code. Forbid photography, 3D renders, gradients, drop shadows, paper texture, grain, noise, vignette, neon, purple, magenta, robots, mascots, humanoid figures, fake IDE windows and brand logos.

angles.title: One playbook. Many repos.
angles.audience: engineering leaders responsible for repeatable maintenance across repositories
angles.insight: Leaders have repeatable maintenance work, many repositories, and review capacity as the real constraint.
angles.hypothesis: We believe framing repeatable maintenance as one playbook fanned across repositories, with review retained by the team, will lower cost per qualified meeting versus generic agent-fleet messaging.

evidence.label: synthesis / interpretation (INT)
evidence.reading: This is the research pack's synthesis of how backlog work becomes parallel across repositories; it is not a customer outcome, a throughput claim, or evidence of Devin's results in any codebase.

measurement.definition_note: Before launch, agree the qualification definition: role, team size, repository ownership, and who confirms the meeting held.
